summary: Host-native filesystem paths, explicit lexical flavours, and portable logical components
lead:
Default `Path` and `path.*` use the execution host: Windows drive, UNC, device and verbatim rules on Windows, and POSIX rules elsewhere. Construction and `toString` preserve exact text. `sep` and `delimiter` are runtime-initialized string constants. `hasRoot` differs from `isAbsolute`, which means fully qualified. `join` preserves dot segments; only `normalize` performs lexical cleanup. `relative` returns `Path?`, with null for incompatible or uncertain roots. `resolve` makes a locator absolute without requiring it to exist; `io.realpath` queries a real filesystem object and `readlink` preserves the link target text.

Import `"std/path/posix"` or `"std/path/windows"` for independent `PosixPath`/`WindowsPath` and their Info types. These pure lexical types have no implicit conversion to filesystem Path. Their nullable `resolve(base, ...parts)` requires an explicit fully-qualified base and never queries cwd. Windows drive-relative input needing another drive's context returns null in the pure module.

Import `"std/path/logical"` for immutable `LogicalPath`. Both `logical.from` and `LogicalPath.from` validate a relative slash-separated component sequence; empty input is legal, but roots, empty components, dot components, backslash and NUL are refused. A colon may occur in logical text. `logical.join` treats empty paths as identity. `logical.toNative(root, value)` requires an explicit absolute host Path and checks each component's host representability; Windows refuses drive/ADS injection, forbidden characters, trailing dot/space and reserved device names. No implicit IO conversion, filesystem-existence check, symlink resolution or sandbox/containment guarantee is provided.
